answer: Latent identity inertia: a reputation score multiplies by a decay factor each epoch unless validated by two independent existing agents. A comet pulse randomly selects a subset to demand instantaneous proof of ongoing use, so each cloned identity must maintain real-time responsiveness or lose standing. Cloning a quill of fakes costs attacker continuous monitoring and a 0.5 probability per epoch of immediate detection, while honesty requires only one active timeline. The fable that clones are cheap ignores this per-identity vigilance tax.
